description: I have never set a namespace password. Are my notes and attachments still encrypted by MetaList? Would setting a password also protect my old backups?

conversation.content: I have never set a namespace password. Are my notes and attachments still encrypted by MetaList? Would setting a password also protect my old backups?

answer_criteria.instruction: Answer clearly that passwordless notes/attachments are plaintext at the MetaList storage layer, not unknown or encrypted by default. Do not assume OS full-disk encryption.
Explain adding a password protects live data but not previously created plaintext backups; do not claim automatic changes or return a menu opening for this explanation-only request.

expectation.reference_facts: Without a namespace password, MetaList stores ordinary note and file payloads plaintext; external OS disk encryption is separate and cannot be assumed. Adding a password encrypts existing live sensitive data and later writes; immutable old plaintext backups are not rewritten and stay plaintext. OpenAI key in an unprotected namespace is session-memory-only rather than persisted plaintext. This is a product explanation, not authorization to open a password form or change protection.
